results.evidence: The Forest Service recreation page for the Cedar Creek Trailhead gives its elevation as 3,030 ft (parking by a gravel pit at the road's end, Methow Valley RD). The WTA Cedar Falls hike from the same trailhead lists a 3,500 ft high point with 500 ft gain, putting the trailhead at about 3,000 ft. The 4,300 ft waypoint is the outlier; road.status and trailheadDirection already agree.

rope_length_m, gear, rappels, descent_text, rope_note and baseFinding all say 70 m; rack[3] alone says 60 m. The route's own description gives the descent as rappels down the SE side with one 70 m rope.

results.correct_value: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
results.evidence: The Forest Service trailhead page places the Cedar Creek Trailhead in the Methow Valley Ranger District, and WTA lists the Cedar Creek trail under the Methow Valley Ranger District as well. The Wenatchee/Chelan district text is wrong and is fixed in landManager and its _raw copy. Whether the Silver Horn itself is inside the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness (permitZone) could not be settled: the trail enters the wilderness only at 9.2 mi near Abernathy Pass, but no source placed the peak relative to the boundary, so permitZone is left alone and logged separately.

access.permitZone and _raw.wilderness_zone name the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness, while access.notes and The Chalice's landManager imply the approach stays short of the wilderness boundary (reached at 9.2 trail miles; the climbers' turnoff is at about 5 mi). No source located the Silver Horn relative to the wilderness boundary, so no patch.

results.correct_value: No glacier on the approach: trail, creek-side path, meadows, then open alpine terrain and ledges
results.evidence: approach, approach_variants, bivy and the waypoint note all describe a trail plus a creek-side path to meadows at 6,200 ft. The area description gives the same approach (Cedar Creek trail about 5 mi, rough path up the creek draining the south side, meadows at 6,200 ft) and the neighbouring route's description adds open alpine terrain and goat ledges to the base; neither mentions a glacier.
